name: TradingRangeVsTrendEntryBias
quote: When the market is clearly bullish, buying near the high and exiting higher is an effective strategy... When it is in a trading range, buying near the high is usually a mistake, and traders should instead try to buy near the low.
description: Switches entry bias by market regime: in a trend, buy strength (near recent highs) and sell weakness (near recent lows); in a trading range, buy near the range low and sell near the range high (invert the bias).
pseudocode: isTrending() ? (buyNearRecentHigh() ; sellNearRecentLow()) : (buyNearRangeLow() ; sellNearRangeHigh())

complexity.reason: requires a trend-vs-trading-range classifier, one of the qualitative design decisions Brooks leaves undefined

chapter_title: The Best Trades: Putting It All Together

name: TradingRangeDayAvoidBuyingNearTopSellingNearBottom
quote: if it is a trading range day, don't look to buy after a strong bull trend bar or a high 1 near the top of the range, and don't look to short after a strong bear trend bar or low 1 near the bottom of the range.
description: On a trading-range day, block long entries (even a strong-looking bull trend bar or high-1 setup) when price is near the top of the day's range, and block short entries near the bottom of the range -- range logic favors selling high and buying low, not chasing toward the extremes.
pseudocode: !(isTradingRangeDay && (close[0] - dayLow) / (dayHigh - dayLow) >= 1 - nearRangeFraction)

complexity.reason: depends on a trading-range-day classification (a research-grade concept elsewhere in this corpus) plus the day's high/low; the range-position ratio itself is trivial once those exist

notes: This chapter is a list of 78 mostly psychological/discipline/money-management guidelines; only those with an actual bar-level test are recorded as candidates here. The rest are grouped in `rejected` below rather than itemized 78 times.

name: TradingRangeFadeAfterMultiBarMove
quote: it is better to only look to short if you are uncertain and the market is up for five to 10 bars, and only look for longs when it is down for five to 10 bars.
description: In an uncertain (trading-range) market, only permit fade-style short entries after price has moved up for roughly 5 to 10 consecutive bars, and only permit fade-style long entries after it has moved down for roughly 5 to 10 consecutive bars.
pseudocode: isTradingRange && consecutiveBarsMovingUp(0, lookback) >= minBarsMoved -> permit short-side fade entries
book_order_type: n/a (an entry-permission gate for countertrend fade setups)

complexity.reason: needs a trading-range classification (research-grade) plus a persistence counter for directional bar movement

name: BarbwirePattern
quote: barbwire A trading range of three or more bars that largely overlap and one or more is a doji.
description: Context filter/primitive: classify the last N bars as barbwire -- heavily overlapping ranges containing at least one doji -- used to block breakout entries. T07-32 references barbwire without formally defining it; this is the formal source.
pseudocode: for k in 0..barbwireBars-2: (min(high[k],high[k+1]) - max(low[k],low[k+1])) >= overlapFraction * range(k); && exists k in 0..barbwireBars-1: abs(body(k)) <= dojiBodyFraction * range(k)

complexity.reason: 'largely overlap' needs a design decision, matching T07-07 TradingRangeContext's note

name: MarketInTradingRange
quote: the market is moving sideways and not covering many points... an extreme trading range where every one- or two-tick up move is followed by a one- or two-tick down move and vice versa.
description: Primitive: approximate 'the market is in a trading range' as the last rangeBars bars largely overlapping (each pair's overlap at least a fraction of its range), i.e. little net progress.
pseudocode: for k in 0..rangeBars-1: (min(high[k],high[k+1]) - max(low[k],low[k+1])) >= overlapFraction * range(k) -> inTradingRange

complexity.reason: 'trading range' is a design decision; bar-overlap is one workable proxy

notes: Same primitive family as TradingRangeContext defined in other chapters of this book; expected to merge in dedup.
chapter_title: The Spectrum of Price Action: Extreme Trends to Extreme Trading Ranges

name: TradingRangeContext
quote: there is usually more overlap of the bars, more small pullbacks, more bars with tails, and some bear trend bars.
description: Primitive context filter: the market is in a trading range, approximated as the last N bars each largely overlapping the prior bar. Used to block breakout entries and to permit the fade/test setups this chapter describes.
pseudocode: for k in 0..rangeBars-1: (min(high[k],high[k+1]) - max(low[k],low[k+1])) >= overlapFraction * min(range(k),range(k+1)) -> inTradingRange; filter passes when !inTradingRange

complexity.reason: 'trading range' is a design decision (Brooks's own definition also involves slope and reversal count); overlap is one workable proxy

notes: Redefines the same primitive chapter 7 (T07-07) defines; the dedup pass should merge them.
chapter_title: Breakouts, Trading Ranges, Tests, and Reversals

name: TrendingTradingRangeDayReversalContext
quote: Most reversal bars on the daily chart come from trending trading range days ... Whenever traders see a trending trading range day, they should be aware that it might have a strong reversal later in the day.
description: Context filter: on a trending trading range day, favor reversal-bar entries later in the session (a permissive rather than blocking filter). Day-type classification itself is deferred to Chapter 22.
pseudocode: tradingRangeDay -> allowReversalEntries

complexity.reason: 'trending trading range day' classification is a design decision, not yet defined

name: TradingRangeContext
quote: every outside bar is a part of a trading range, which is two or more bars that largely overlap.
description: Primitive context filter: the market is in a trading range, approximated as the last N bars each overlapping the prior bar by at least a fraction of their range (largely overlapping bars). Used to block breakout entries.
pseudocode: for k in 0..rangeBars-1: (min(high[k],high[k+1]) - max(low[k],low[k+1])) >= overlapFraction * range(k) -> inTradingRange; filter passes when !inTradingRange

complexity.reason: 'trading range' is a design decision; the overlap count is one workable proxy but Brooks's notion also involves multiple reversals and a flat EMA

notes: ADX below a threshold is the corpus's nearest existing low-trend proxy.

name: LongLegOnTradingRangeDayFade
quote: this was a trading range day and any time a leg lasts more than five bars, traders will be looking for a reversal
description: On a trading range day, when the current leg has lasted more than N bars (e.g., N consecutive bars without a lower low being taken out), allow countertrend (fade) entries only.
pseudocode: tradingRangeDay && legLengthBars(up) > legBars -> allow short / block long

complexity.reason: 'trading range day' classification and leg length both need design decisions

name: EarlyReversalsMarkTradingRangeDay
quote: Multiple reversals, big tails, and uncertainty are all characteristics of trading range days
description: If the first N bars of the session contain at least K reversals (alternating trend bars) and mostly tailed bars, classify the day as a trading range day: scalp, fade extremes, do not swing.
pseudocode: sessionBar <= N && countDirectionChanges(sessionBars) >= K && avgTailFraction(sessionBars) >= tailMin -> tradingRangeDay

complexity.reason: day-type classification carried across the session is a design decision

name: LargeOverlapSignalsTradingRange
quote: the second, third, and fourth bars were large and almost entirely overlapping, and this is a sign of uncertainty, one of the hallmarks of a trading range.
description: When consecutive large bars overlap heavily (their ranges mostly coincide), treat the market as two-sided/trading-range rather than trending, and discount trend-line breakout signals formed by such bars.
pseudocode: (min(high[0], high[1]) - max(low[0], low[1])) >= overlapFraction * min(high[0] - low[0], high[1] - low[1]) && (high[0] - low[0]) >= largeBarAtrMultiple * atr(atrLength)

complexity.reason: a two-bar overlap ratio plus an ATR size test

notes: Opposite reading of the LittleOverlap primitive used elsewhere for spike bars (large overlap here signals a range, not a spike).

name: TradingRangeDayContext
quote: Most days are trading range days or have a lot of trading range activity. On these days you will find that horizontal lines across swing highs and lows often serve as barriers that result in failed breakouts and then reversals.
description: Gate T17-02/T17-03 on the day being a trading-range day rather than a trend day; on trend days horizontal lines should instead be used only for with-trend pullback entries (T17-05).
pseudocode: !isTrendDay

complexity.reason: 'trading range day' vs. 'trend day' is a discretionary daily-scale judgment with no single bar-level test given; a proxy (e.g., TrendingSwings false, or a Donchian-band-hug test) is a design decision

chapter_title: Horizontal Lines: Swing Points and Other Key Price Levels

name: LargePullbacksMeanTradingRange
quote: Once a strong bull begins to have pullbacks that are relatively large, the pullbacks... behave more like trading ranges than bull flags... A new high is now a breakout attempt above a trading range, and the odds are that it will fail.
description: Filter: the depth of the most recent pullback (last swing high minus the subsequent lowest low) relative to the preceding leg's height is below maxPullbackFraction; otherwise breakout buys above the old high are blocked (expected to fail).
pseudocode: (lastSwingHigh - lowest(low, barsSinceLastSwingHigh)[0]) / (lastSwingHigh - priorSwingLow) < maxPullbackFraction

complexity.reason: leg height needs swing pivots

notes: Page 314: 'Every trading range is within either a bull trend or a bear trend'; while in the range the trend 'is no longer strong'.

name: PullbackOverTenBarsIsTradingRange
quote: The second possibility occurs if the pullback extends for more than 10 bars. It will then have grown into a trading range, which can break out in either direction.
description: Filter: after a spike, if the pullback has lasted more than N bars without a new extreme, the spike-and-channel expectation is off and the pullback is treated as a trading range (entries in either direction; with-trend breakout slightly favored).
pseudocode: spikeEnded && (barIndex - spikeEndBar) > rangeBars && highest(high, barIndex - spikeEndBar) <= spikeEndHigh

complexity.reason: counter against the spike state machine
